# ShotZ 0.1.2
Fixes for the editor's Background panel, and a privacy and security tidy-up.
- Sliders in the editor now follow the pointer. Padding, Corners, Angle, Opacity, Corner radius and Redaction strength used to jump to the end and stick there. - Position in the Background panel now moves the image, with any aspect. When there is no room to move it, the grid is greyed out and says why. - Saving a Background preset works: the name field is ready for typing, and Save waits until you have typed a name. - Your captures, documents and history are now stored so that only your user account can read them. Existing files are tightened the first time 0.1.2 starts; files you save or export are not affected. - ShotZ's log entries no longer show file names or paths. - The app no longer contains file paths from the computer it was built on. - Developer test switches are ignored by the released app. - Settings ▸ Advanced has a new Acknowledgements row with the licences for ShotZ and the open-source software it includes.

# ShotZ 0.1.1
A small follow-up to the first release.
- New app icon. - Clicking a switch, button or other control no longer leaves a blue focus ring around it. The ring now appears only when you move between controls with the keyboard (Tab). - The Screen Recording step now explains what to do if ShotZ appears twice in System Settings after updating from an earlier build. - Settings ▸ Advanced shows the new version, 0.1.1. - Internal: release checks for the signing team, and safer tests.

# ShotZ 0.1.0
The first public release of ShotZ.
- Capture an area, a window or the full screen with your shortcuts. - The quick-access stack keeps every capture at hand: copy, save, drag out or annotate. - Annotate with arrows, shapes, text, counters, highlights and redaction, then copy or save. - Present captures on a background with padding, gradients and shadow.
